name: Escapement
desc: A clock movement plate where a Graham deadbeat escapement actually works — the escape wheel sits dead still under the pallets, then runs exactly half a tooth as the pendulum sweeps through centre, the going train grinds round behind at its real reductions, the mainspring uncoils in the barrel, and a live oscillogram traces the arc along the bottom of the sheet.

energy.doc: line weight + pendulum arc + inspection-wash glow + plate drift

scale.doc: movement size — 1.9 zooms into the escaping teeth

density.doc: how much of the going train is drawn behind (3..5 wheels: fourth, third, centre, motion, barrel)

speed.doc: beat rate — how fast the clock is being driven

hue.doc: plate tint (film/ghost styles); other styles are fixed inks

y.doc: suspension point — the movement hangs below it

anno.doc: annotation density: centrelines, swing envelope, dial, oscillogram, title block

style.doc: aesthetic: toned drafting film / prussian cyanotype / aged engraved plate / additive x-ray ghost / schematic (wheels reduce to pitch circles and the beat trace becomes the subject)

seed.doc: escape-wheel tooth count (30/32/36/40) and plate grain

alpha.doc: ink opacity over the plate ground
